title: When Do Agent Loops Mistake Stagnation for Progress? Self-Evaluation Bias and Externally Grounded Verification in Long-Running Autonomous LLM Agent Loops
abstract: arXiv:2607.25152v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Long-running autonomous agents plan, act, and judge their own completion without human intervention. When an agent grades its own work, self-evaluation bias takes hold: plausible changes are accepted as progress while real-world outcomes stagnate or regress. We name this failure mode the progress mirage and show, with controlled measurement, that it is a question of what the evaluator is grounded in. We built a testbed that holds the agent and its tool surface fixed and manipulates only the information-channel type of the evaluator that gates the loop. A world-state oracle, unfakeable in principle, is enforced by container and network isolation and verified at every run. Across 54 cycles a frontier agent claimed improvement every time, yet 56 percent had a measured delta of zero or below. Self-report was thus uninformative, and the self-verdict gate degenerated into accept-all, eroding the best deployed state it had reached by 19 per

translated_title: 智能体循环何时将停滞误认为进步？长时运行自主大语言模型智能体循环中的自我评估偏差与外部锚定验证
translated_abstract: arXiv:2607.25152v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：长时运行的自主智能体在无需人工干预的情况下进行规划、行动，并自行判断任务是否完成。当智能体为自己的工作评分时，自我评估偏差便会产生：看似合理的变更被当作进步接受，而现实世界的结果却停滞不前甚至倒退。我们将这种失效模式命名为“进步海市蜃楼”，并通过受控测量表明，这实际上是一个评估者所依据信息基础的问题。我们构建了一个测试平台，保持智能体及其工具接口固定不变，仅操控门控循环的评估器的信息通道类型。一个原则上不可伪造的世界状态预言机由容器与网络隔离强制实施，并在每次运行时进行验证。在54个循环中，一个前沿智能体每次都声称取得了改进，但其中56%的循环实测增量为零或以下。因此，自我报告不具参考价值，自我裁决门退化成了“全部接受”，使其已达到的最佳部署状态被侵蚀了19%……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 长时运行自主LLM智能体循环中存在“进步海市蜃楼”失效模式——智能体每轮都自评有进展，但实测56%的循环无改进甚至倒退，只有将评估锚定在不可伪造的外部世界状态预言机上，才能有效消除这种自我评估偏差。
en_tdlr: Long-running autonomous LLM agent loops suffer from a "progress mirage" failure mode—agents claim improvement every cycle while 56% of measured deltas are zero or negative—and only externally grounded verification through an unfakeable world-state oracle effectively eliminates this self-evaluation bias.
